title: Nashville: the car that has waited nine days; its owner writes for the fourth time
demonstrates: A web chat: the assistant answers first, cannot read the shop system and hands the question over; from the advisor's first line the chat is his and the assistant only drafts. The weak desk in writing: replies at closing time, a handful of words, a new date each time and no reason. Every draft is discarded. A private note by the other advisor says what is really going on, and the manager's answer to it is one word. At T the fourth message is unanswered, the chat is Urgent by its wait, and a usable draft sits in the box.

scenario.who_writes: A customer whose car has stood at the Charlotte Pike shop since T-9d, waiting for a part.
scenario.waiting_for: a remanufactured angle gear, ordered from the supplier the shop kept after the purchase, promised twice and moved twice
scenario.what_happens: He writes 7, 5, 3 and 1 days before T and phones on T-4d and T-1d (calls design, story calls 15 and 16). Chad answers three times, late, with a date or with nothing. Jasmine asks the manager in a note to order through the home shops' parts manager or tell the customer the truth. The manager writes 'handled'. Nothing changes.

timeline.text: Morning. Curtis Vaughn, you have my Volvo XC60. I was told the part would be in today. Any word?

Good morning, Mr. Vaughn. I'm the assistant for Brennan Auto Care. I can't see the shop's repair orders from here, so I don't have the status of your part. I'll pass your question to the service desk at the Charlotte Pike shop so they can answer you. What's the best number to reach you?
Thank you. Your question is with the team now, and somebody will get back to you as soon as possible.

why: Chad's three replies are twenty-five words together and none of them says why.
The customer goes from 'Morning.' to counting days and money; he never swears in writing.
The note is the only place the supplier is named, and it sits two lines above 'handled'.
The drafts get better as the customer gets angrier, and the outcome rows say nobody used one.
new_facts: The first date, Friday, was given to him when the part was ordered, on the day after the car came in, outside the chat and outside any hand-written call (call 15: 'Fella told me Friday').

ERP: the purchase order for the angle gear was promised for 7 days before T, then for west's 4th full open day before T; on the day of message 3 the supplier said 'early next week' with no tracking number.
Chad repeated call 15's promise in writing at 17:21 on the day of the call.
He has a rental car since 8 days before T.
The missed call is at 09:12 and call 16 at 14:20, as story call 16 has them; message 4 is written after call 16.
